topics.label: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)
topics.metaDescription: PGWP eligibility for 2026: field-of-study rules, permit length by program duration, and how it connects to CEC and permanent residence.
topics.lead: A PGWP is an open work permit for international graduates of eligible Canadian programs, and is the most common bridge between a study permit and permanent residence through the Canadian Experience Class. Since November 2024, PGWP eligibility depends on having studied in a field IRCC considers aligned with labour market needs.

topics.label: International Experience Canada (IEC)
topics.seoTitle: International Experience Canada (IEC) 2026: Working Holiday | CMG
topics.metaDescription: IEC / Working Holiday Canada 2026: eligible countries, pool entry, and the three category types explained. Age limits and application timing.
topics.lead: International Experience Canada is a reciprocal program allowing young adults from partner countries to work in Canada temporarily — most commonly through the Working Holiday category, an open work permit not tied to a single employer. Eligibility depends entirely on citizenship, as each partner country has its own agreement and annual quota with Canada.

topics.label: LMIA & Employer Services (overview)
topics.seoTitle: LMIA & Employer Immigration Services Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: LMIA support for Canadian employers: all streams, Global Talent Stream, ESDC compliance. Audit-ready files from a licensed RCIC team. Free consultation.
topics.lead: Whether it's a single high-wage hire or a seasonal agricultural crew, the LMIA process runs on documented recruitment, defensible wage benchmarking, and compliance records employers can produce years later on demand.

topics.label: Global Talent Stream
topics.seoTitle: Global Talent Stream Canada 2026: Fast-Track Work Permits | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Global Talent Stream for employers: Category A & B eligibility, the 2-week processing target, and how it compares to standard LMIA streams.
topics.lead: The Global Talent Stream is an expedited LMIA stream for employers hiring in-demand tech and specialized talent roles, built around a significantly faster processing target than standard LMIA categories.
headings: How to Choose the Right GTS Category

topics.label: TFWP Employer Compliance
topics.seoTitle: TFWP Employer Compliance Canada 2026: Audit Readiness | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Employer compliance obligations under Canada's Temporary Foreign Worker Program — recordkeeping, wage rules, and inspection preparation.
topics.lead: Employers hiring through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program take on ongoing compliance obligations that extend well past the LMIA approval itself — ESDC can inspect an employer's records at any point during, and for years after, a foreign worker's employment.

topics.label: Spousal & Partner Sponsorship (overview)
topics.seoTitle: Spousal Sponsorship Canada 2026: Inland vs Outland | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Sponsor a spouse or partner for Canadian PR. Inland vs outland routes, relationship evidence, and open work permit eligibility. Free consultation.
topics.lead: Spousal sponsorship is the route for Canadian citizens and permanent residents to sponsor a spouse, common-law partner, or conjugal partner for permanent residence. Applications are decided primarily on whether the relationship is genuine and ongoing — documentation quality matters as much as the underlying facts.

topics.label: Spousal / Common-Law Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Sponsor a spouse or common-law partner for Canadian PR. Eligibility differences between married and common-law status. Free assessment.
topics.lead: This covers the two most common relationship categories in spousal sponsorship: legally married spouses, and common-law partners who have cohabited continuously for at least 12 months. Both routes lead to the same permanent residence outcome, but the evidence required differs slightly.

topics.label: Conjugal Partner Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Conjugal partner sponsorship for couples unable to marry or cohabit due to exceptional circumstances — eligibility and evidence explained.
topics.lead: Conjugal partner sponsorship exists for couples in a committed relationship comparable to marriage or common-law status, but who have been unable to marry or live together continuously due to significant, often legal or immigration-related, barriers outside their control.
